notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase, mostly general vs a stage (before-course, during-work, over-time) for rationale, principle and evidence statements; resolved to general when the passage is not tied to a course stage. (2) actor, admin vs all or instructor for reported committee findings and for office-provided resources; resolved by who the sentence binds or who acts (the office that provides a resource is admin). (3) policy_type, mostly P63 vs P04 for syllabus templates (P63), P56 vs P02/UNCOVERED/P36 for framework principles (P56 when the sentence is a principle about how the University frames rules), P45 vs P36 for the aid-vs-collaborator boundary, and UNCOVERED vs P09 for the duty to explain reasons for AI rules (kept UNCOVERED) and for AI-literacy curriculum items (UNCOVERED). (4) modality, informs vs should/must where a sentence only describes a charge, a pilot or a code's coverage (informs). (5) unit_stance, restrict/require vs neutral/permit: disclosure and code-compliance duties are conditions on permitted use, so permit or neutral, not require. Units found by one coder: A over-coded survey counts, peer or literature summaries and pilot descriptions, which were dropped (34 only_A, 16 kept: real principles, open questions for the codes, and recommendations); B's 19 only_B (11 kept: distinct study-aid, prompt-history and framework statements). Coder splits of one sentence were merged, and a few mis-aligned pairs were re-paired by passage. Stance agreed on all 4 documents (all delegates). Shares are computed over matched units after re-pairing.
